project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - TOTAL of 4 ROD-approved tracts
source_quote: ROD NOAs: North Hilight 467,596,000; South Porcupine 401,830,508; North Porcupine 721,154,828 tons of mineable Federal coal; South Hilight sale notice 222,676,000
notes: DERIVED SUM of the 4 ROD-approved tracts (Alternative 2 configurations). value_high = Proposed Action as-applied total for all six tracts. Of the ROD total, 1,345.66 Mt was actually leased (row R1154i). As-applied total for all six tracts in FEIS = 2,435.4 Mt recoverable (263.4+213.6+377.9+669.6+601.2+309.7); ROD-selected total for the 4 tracts with RODs = 1,813.3 Mt (adds unsold North Hilight 467.6 Mt). West Hilight and West Jacobs Ranch never got RODs. Maintenance tracts: extend life of existing Black Thunder and North Antelope Rochelle mines at the same production rate (no production increase), hence continuation.

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - North Hilight Field (WYW164812, Ark Land/Arch, Black Thunder)
source_quote: Under Alternative 2... The LBA area includes approximately 4,530 acres. The BLM estimates that it contains approximately 467,596,000 tons of mineable Federal coal reserves

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - South Hilight Field (WYW174596, Ark Land/Arch, Black Thunder)

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - West Hilight Field (WYW172388, Ark Land/Arch, Black Thunder)

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - North Porcupine (WYW173408, BTU Western/Peabody, North Antelope Rochelle)

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - South Porcupine (WYW176095, BTU Western/Peabody, North Antelope Rochelle)

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - production rate of affected mines
source_quote: the new leases will maintain the same production at these mines as in the past: 135 million tons per year at Black Thunder and 95 million tons per year at North Antelope Rochelle, for a total of 230 million tons per year
notes: This is TOTAL mine production (both mines), not the production attributable to the leases. 10th Cir (citing FEIS): North/South Hilight extend Black Thunder ~4 years; North/South Porcupine extend NARM ~9 years (mine_life_extension_years). Note 10th Cir. 4-yr Hilight figure includes unsold North Hilight.

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - FEIS combustion CO2
source_quote: the quantity of coal proposed in these leases would result in approximately 382 million tons of annual carbon dioxide emissions from electricity generation, id. at 987, which is the equivalent of roughly 6% of the United States's total emissions in 2008
notes: From 10th Cir. opinion quoting FEIS p.987; corresponds to the 230 Mt/yr combined mine output (~1.66 t CO2/t coal), i.e. total-mine combustion, not incremental. Unit ambiguous: sanity check 230 Mst coal x ~8,900 Btu/lb x ~97 kgCO2/MMBtu = ~395 Mt metric (~435 M short tons), so 382 is closer to METRIC tonnes; if short tons, = 347 Mt metric. Confidence on unit: medium. SUBSTITUTION: FEIS assumed perfect substitution (no-action = same national emissions); 10th Cir (WildEarth Guardians v. BLM, 870 F.3d 1222, 2017) held this arbitrary and capricious, remanded without vacatur. BLM remand EA DOI-BLM-WY-P000-2018-0002-EA (draft Jul 2018, final+FONSI 3 Jun 2019) reaffirmed leasing; Policy Integrity says it 'doubles down' on substitution. Remand EA net-emissions numbers NOT FOUND (ePlanning PDF links dead).

project_name: Buckskin Mine Hay Creek II Coal Lease (WYW172684, Kiewit)
source_quote: The tract contains an estimated 167,001,577 tons of mineable coal. ... average quality on an as-received basis is 8,297 British Thermal Units
notes: ROD (1 May 2013) Alternative 2: 1,253.27 acres, ~167 Mt mineable. NOT SOLD: sale 9/18/2013, sole bid $35,070,331 ($0.21/ton) rejected (BLM PRB unsuccessful sales table); no later sale in BLM successful-sales table. value_low = applicant's modified 419-acre tract 54.1 Mt (DEIS NOA). Heat content 8,297 Btu/lb. Buckskin mine itself continues operating on existing leases.

project_name: Buckskin Mine Hay Creek II - production rate / mine life
source_quote: At the mining rate of 25 million tons per year, the coal included in the Hay Creek II Tract would extend the life of the Buckskin Mine by as many as 6 years.
notes: NOI (2007, 148 Mt as-applied tract). Air permit cap (not an EIS alternative) 'mine up to 42 million tons of coal per year' (DEIS NOA 2010). mine_life_extension_years ~6 (NOI); derived ~6.7 yr for ROD 167 Mt at 25 Mt/yr. No GHG numbers retrieved from FEIS (NOT FOUND).

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - TOTAL actually leased (South Hilight, North Porcupine, South Porcupine)
source_quote: Tons offered per sale notice: South Porcupine 401,830,508; South Hilight Field 222,676,000; North Porcupine 721,154,828 (all listed as successful sales, leases issued 2012)
notes: Derived sum. Total bonus bids $1.539B. North Hilight (467.6 Mt) approved but never sold; West Hilight and West Jacobs Ranch never reached ROD.

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - mine life extension, Black Thunder (North+South Hilight)
source_quote: the North and South Hilight leases will extend the life of the Black Thunder mine by approximately four years
notes: Per 10th Cir. citing FEIS, at 135 Mt/yr. Only South Hilight (222.7 Mt) was leased: derived ~1.6 yr at 135 Mt/yr. North Hilight never sold.

project_name: Wright Area Coal Lease Project (six PRB tracts) - mine life extension, North Antelope Rochelle (North+South Porcupine)
source_quote: the North and South Porcupine leases will extend the life of the North Antelope Rochelle mine by approximately nine years
notes: Per 10th Cir. citing FEIS, at 95 Mt/yr (1,123 Mt leased / 95 = ~11.8 yr derived, so FEIS 9 yr may reflect different tonnage basis). Actual recent NARM/Black Thunder output is well below the 95/135 Mt/yr analyzed (not checked against EIA here), so as-analyzed CO2 overstates as-operating.

project_name: Buckskin Mine Hay Creek II - mine life extension
source_quote: the coal included in the Hay Creek II Tract would extend the life of the Buckskin Mine by as many as 6 years
notes: NOI figure for the 148 Mt as-applied tract; derived 6.7 yr for ROD 167 Mt at 25 Mt/yr. Moot: lease never sold (bid rejected 2013).

project_name: Four Corners Power Plant and Navajo Mine Energy Project - FCPP Units 4&5
source_quote: total generating capability of 2,100 MW: Unit 1, 170 net MW, in service from 1962 to December 2013... Unit 3, 220 net MW... Unit 4, 770 net MW, in service since 1969; Unit 5, 770 net MW, in service since 1970
notes: NET MW (gross EIA-860 nameplate NOT FOUND/not checked; likely somewhat higher). FEIS Sec. 2.2 (May 2015). Units 1-3 (560 MW) retired Dec 2013 (pre-retirement total 2,100 MW). ROD (80 FR 43116, 21 Jul 2015): 'two energy generation units producing approximately 1,500 megawatts'; lease extended 25 years to 2041. Fuel: Navajo Mine low-rank coal (target 8,700-8,750 Btu/lb). Capacity factor analyzed: future max 92%, historic avg 84-86%. CCS considered as an alternative only; capture_rate = 0. Oct 2026: operating; APS 2020 plan was exit by 2031, but a Sept 2026 APS-NTEC agreement could extend operation to 2038 (KJZZ 5 Oct 2026; medium).

project_name: Four Corners Power Plant - EIS annual CO2e (Units 4&5, post-2018)
source_quote: Table 2-8... CO2 Equivalents (CO2e) 15,439,236 [historic Units 1-5] 11,396,710 [estimated future post-2018, Units 4 and 5] 26% ... Future maximum annual capacity factor = 92 percent
notes: Table 2-8 says 'tons/yr' without short/metric. Sanity check: 2 units x 7,411 MMBtu/hr x 8,760 h x 0.92 x ~97 kgCO2/MMBtu = ~11.6 Mt METRIC, so 11.40 is most consistent with metric tonnes (EPA-sourced data); if short tons it would be 10.34 Mt metric. Historic 2005-11 baseline (5 units) 15.44 M tons/yr. Plant combustion only. Confidence medium on unit, high on the number.

project_name: Four Corners/Navajo Mine - Navajo Mine (new Pinabete permit + existing permit) coal supply
source_quote: The proposed Pinabete Permit area would, in conjunction with the mining of any reserves remaining within the existing Navajo Mine Permit area... supply low-sulfur coal to the FCPP at a rate of approximately 5.8 million tons per year
notes: OSMRE ROD (FR 21 Jul 2015). New 5,659-acre Pinabete permit area (2,744 acres mined). mine_life_extension_years = 25 ('supply coal to FCPP for up to 25 years beginning in 2016'). Implied total ~145 Mt over 25 yr (derived). Prior output with 5 units: 8,967,000 tons in 2009 (FEIS Table 2-4). In-situ heat content 7,800-9,500 Btu/lb. Coal combustion CO2 is the FCPP row (R0334b), do not double count. NOTE: OSMRE separately approved a NEW NTEC 'No Name' SMCRA permit (EIS NOI Jan 2026, ROD Jul 2026; ~9,042 acres, ~5 Mt/yr per search summary, unverified) - later action outside this EIS.

project_name: Deer Creek Station (Basin Electric, gas combined cycle, Brookings County SD)
source_quote: The proposed Project has been sized for 300 MW in order to meet the 250 MW intermediate power supply need and have a 50 MW reserve to meet peak intermediate needs.
notes: Natural gas combined cycle (one GE 7FA CT + steam turbine with duct firing per trade press). Intermediate-load unit (EIS: 20-80% CF class) but GHG table assumes 8,760 hr/yr. Commercial operation Aug 2012 per Basin Electric 10-yr plan filed with SD PUC (search snippet; medium). Value from DEIS (WAPA); FEIS not opened (rd.usda.gov link dead). 2026 operating status not independently verified.

project_name: Deer Creek Station - EIS annual CO2e
source_quote: The operation of the 300-MW Deer Creek Station would release an estimated 1.02 million tons of CO2 equivalent (0.93 million metric tons) into the atmosphere each year (table 4-2).
notes: Metric tonnes stated explicitly. Table 4-2 assumes CT (1,434 MMBtu/hr) and duct burner (610.4 MMBtu/hr) at 8,760 hr/yr, i.e. a potential-to-emit upper bound (100% CF); actual intermediate-duty emissions lower. capture_rate 0.

project_name: Groton Generation Station operating-limit removal (Basin Electric, Brown County SD)
source_quote: Groton Generation Station has two generating units. Each unit is powered by a General Electric (GE) LMS100 simple cycle gas turbine rated at 100 MW at design conditions. Unit 1... July 1, 2006, and Unit 2... July 1, 2008.
notes: Existing gas peaker; no construction. Action = WAPA LGIA change removing the 50-MW annual-average limit (ROD Dec 2011). CHANGE: output cap 438,000 MWh/yr (25% CF, = 2,190 full-load station-hours at 200 MW) -> 743,760 MWh/yr (42.5% CF, = 3,718.8 station full-load hours/yr, bound by Title V 238 tpy NOx and CO limits); +305,760 MWh/yr. Full output (1,752,000 MWh) would need PSD modification. Status 2026 assumed operating (not independently verified).

project_name: Groton Generation Station - EIS annual CO2e (with vs without limit)
source_quote: Station GHG Emissions (CO2e) 186,322 mtons CO2e/yr [with 50-MW limit] 318,098 mtons CO2e/yr [without limit] 749,299 mtons CO2e/yr [full output]
notes: Metric tons. low = No Action (50-MW limit), central = proposed action. INCREMENTAL emissions from the federal action = 131,776 tCO2e/yr (derived). ES text says 187,322 for no-action vs Table 2.1 186,322 (internal EIS inconsistency, 1,000 t).

project_name: Kemper County IGCC (Mississippi Power / Southern Co.)
source_quote: the Kemper County IGCC Project would generate a nominal 582 MW (net) of electricity when duct firing natural gas (for supplemental energy input) in the HRSG
notes: Lignite IGCC (two TRIG gasifiers, 2 CTs + ST) with adjacent Liberty Fuels lignite mine (~4.3 Mt/yr for up to 40 yr, ROD). capture_rate 67% (ROD: 'DOE has decided to fund includes a capture rate of 67 percent'; EIS analysed 25/50/67/>67%). CO2 to EOR. Capacity factor analysed 85%. STATUS: lignite gasification suspended June 2017; gasifier structures imploded Oct 2021; the combined-cycle units continue to operate on NATURAL GAS as Plant Ratcliffe (MS PSC commissioner note, medium). Coal/CCS component = cancelled; gas CC = operating.

project_name: Kemper County IGCC - EIS annual CO2 (after 67% capture)
source_quote: The project, operating at an 85-percent capacity factor (i.e., at full capacity), will emit approximately 1.8 million tpy of CO2 while burning lignite coal and firing natural gas in the duct burners.
notes: ROD also: 'would also emit an estimated 1.8 to 2.6 million tpy of CO2 annually' (range spans capture-rate alternatives); +~91,000 tpy other GHG; +~130,000 t life-cycle support/mining (total ~2.0 Mt). 'tpy' = short tons by US convention (1.8 Mst = 1.63 Mt metric). Lignite feed 13,800 tons/day. As-operated since 2017 the plant is an NGCC with no capture, so actual emissions differ from the EIS case.

project_name: FutureGen 2.0 (Meredosia IL Unit 4 oxy-combustion repowering + CO2 storage)
source_quote: The repowered unit would generate 168 MWe of power (gross) and CO2 suitable for transport by pipeline.
notes: Repowering of existing Ameren Meredosia Unit 4 (retrofit; new_or_existing could also be read as 'new_build' of the oxy-combustion boiler). Fuel: 60% Illinois No. 6 bituminous / 40% PRB blend. capture_rate >=90% (ROD). DOE suspended funding Feb 2015 (Recovery Act deadline Sept 2015); Alliance ceased development Jan 2016 (trade press via search snippets; status confidence medium-low). Never built.

project_name: FutureGen 2.0 - CO2 captured and stored
source_quote: capture at least 90 percent (approximately 1.2 million tons [1.1 million metric tons] annually) of CO2 ... up to a total of 24 million tons (22 million metric tons) over approximately 20 years
notes: Captured, not emitted. Residual stack emissions not extracted (~0.12 Mt/yr if exactly 90%, derived). Net emissions effect of the project is a reduction vs. a conventional unit.

project_name: Texas Clean Energy Project (Summit, IGCC polygen, Odessa/Penwell TX)
source_quote: Summit's TCEP will generate up to 400 megawatts (MW), of which 130 to 213 MW (approximately 1.0 to 1.7 billion net kilowatt-hours of electricity per year) will be available to the electricity grid.
notes: 400 MW GROSS; only 130-213 MW NET to grid (row R1016c; rest used internally incl. urea plant). PRB sub-bituminous coal IGCC with urea production; capture_rate ~90%. DOE notified intent to discontinue cooperative agreement June 2016; terminated thereafter (DOE OIG 2018 audit). Never built. status_year 2016 medium.

project_name: Texas Clean Energy Project - EIS annual CO2 emitted
source_quote: Annual emissions of CO2 from the TCEP operations will range up to 300,000 tons per year
notes: Emitted after capture. Captured: 'up to 3 million tons (2.7 million metric tonnes) of CO2 annually', 2.5-3.0 Mst sold for EOR in Permian Basin. Emissions from urea use and EOR not counted.

project_name: Texas Clean Energy Project - net power to grid
source_quote: of which 130 to 213 MW (approximately 1.0 to 1.7 billion net kilowatt-hours of electricity per year) will be available to the electricity grid
notes: Range stated in ROD; central set to upper bound of the stated range (no single value given). 1.0-1.7 TWh/yr net.

project_name: East Lynn Lake Coal Lease (WVES-50556 Argus + WVES-50560 Rockspring, Wayne County WV)
source_quote: The ELL Argus tract reserve contains 15 million tons of recoverable high-volatile A and B bituminous coal... 12,500-13,200 Btu/lb... The ELL Rockspring tract contains approximately 11 million tons of recoverable
notes: Underground mining from adjacent private mines (Argus, Rockspring); ~13,090 acres beneath USACE East Lynn Lake project lands. ROD 15 Mar 2013. Competitive sale scheduled 4 Dec 2014; OUTCOME NOT FOUND (no follow-up FR notice found; web search budget exhausted). Production rate NOT FOUND in EIS; 2008 Herald-Dispatch said 26.2 Mt over 10-15 years (~1.7-2.6 Mt/yr, derived; medium). Heat content 12,500-13,200 Btu/lb.

project_name: Greens Hollow Coal Lease Tract (UTU-84102, SUFCO mine, Sanpete/Sevier UT)
source_quote: The coal beds contain approximately 73.4 million in-place tons of coal. However... the tract being offered for sale is projected to contain approximately 55.7 million tons of technically recoverable high-volatile C bituminous coal.
notes: 6,175 acres, underground longwall via existing SUFCO mine (applicant Ark Land/Arch, later Canyon Fuel). NOI: extend SUFCO mine life by ~10 years (mine_life_extension_years=10) and 'maintain production'; implied ~5.6 Mt/yr (derived). Heat content 11,538-11,565 Btu/lb. FEIS Dec 2011 had no ROD; Supplemental EIS 2012-2015; sale noticed for 22 Sep 2016, postponed (litigation), reset to 4 Jan 2017. Sale OUTCOME NOT FOUND in sources opened (web search budget exhausted); my unverified recollection is that Canyon Fuel won and the lease was issued - VERIFY. In-place tons 73.4 Mt (not an alternative).

project_name: West Elk Mine lease modifications COC-1362 & COC-67232 (Arch/Mountain Coal, Gunnison County CO) - 2012 FEIS
source_quote: Under Alternative 3, the E seam would be mined containing approximately 10 million tons of recoverable coal... producing approximately 4.5 million tons per year and continuing mining operations by approximately 3 years.
notes: Tonnage from OSMRE 2019 mining-plan ROD describing the 2017 SFEIS Alt 3 (same 1,720-acre modifications); 2012 BLM ROD (Dec 2012) gave no tonnage but 'extend the existing operations approximately 19 months [federal] ... an additional 16-17 months of mining coal on adjacent private lands'. coal_production_rate ~4.5 Mt/yr; mine_life_extension ~3 yr (2017) or ~1.6 yr federal + ~1.4 yr private (2012). 2012 approvals vacated by D. Colo. 2014 (High Country Conservation Advocates v. USFS; social cost of carbon/GHG analysis) -> USFS SFEIS 2017 (not in this list) -> BLM ROD 15 Dec 2017, modifications effective 1 Dec 2017 (BLM table: COC-67232 920 acres, 559,000 tons offered, $167,700 = $0.30/ton). West Elk mine operating. Bituminous; Btu NOT FOUND. Substitution/GHG numbers from SFEIS NOT FOUND.

project_name: Federal Coal Lease Modifications COC-1362 and COC-67232 (BLM ROD, duplicate of R0304)
source_quote: The BLM approves Alternative 3, to modify Mountain Coal Company's existing Federal coal lease COC-1362 by adding 921 acres and the Ark Land Companies existing Federal coal lease COC-67232 by adding 800 acres at the West Elk Mine.
notes: DUPLICATE of R0304: values intentionally blank to avoid double counting; use R0304 (~10 Mt). Same project; R0304 = USFS consent ROD Aug 2012, R0305 = BLM ROD 28 Dec 2012). Do NOT double count. Note the 2012 BLM ROD assigns 921 ac to COC-1362 and 800 ac to COC-67232, opposite of the 2012 NOI and the 2018 BLM table (COC-67232 = 920 ac). The 'redo' is the 2017 USFS SFEIS (FR NOA 8 Sep 2017), not in the CEQ 2010-mid-2018 list as a separate row here.

project_name: Rusk Permit Area - South Hallsville No. 1 Lignite Mine expansion (Sabine Mining Co., for AEP Pirkey plant)
source_quote: The approximately 20,377-acre mine site would recover approximately 130 million tons of lignite during the 30-year life of the mine, for sole use at the existing H.W. Pirkey Power Plant
notes: USACE Section 404 permit (not a federal lease; private lignite). From the 2009 NOI; FEIS (May 2011) not opened. Implied ~4.3 Mt/yr over 30 yr (derived coal_production_rate); mine_life_extension 30 yr. Texas lignite (Btu NOT FOUND). STATUS: from memory only (unverified), AEP/SWEPCO retired Pirkey ~2023, which would end mining; verify before use.

project_name: USACE Fort Worth District Regional EIS for Surface Coal and Lignite Mining in Texas
source_quote: The USACE is undertaking a REIS to streamline the NEPA aspect of the Section 404/10 permitting process... for future coal and lignite mine expansions in Texas subject to permitting by the USACE.
notes: Programmatic Regional EIS (REIS), funded by the Texas Mining and Reclamation Association via third-party contract; DEIS Jul 2015, FEIS Apr 2016, ROD Jan 2017. Covers future Section 404/10 permits for TX surface coal/lignite mine expansions; no specific tonnage. NOT FOUND: list of mines/tonnage covered. Recommend weight zero or treat via the tiered mine-specific permits.
